plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 27: Biomolecules: Lipids
plan.contextChunk: This figure sets a three-dimensional rendering of a lipid bilayer beside the flat structural formula of the molecule that builds it. On the left, a slab of membrane is drawn in perspective with a stepped cutaway at one corner: rows of small green spheres tile the top and bottom faces, and the interior between them is packed with pale tan wavy strands that meet tip to tip along the slab's midplane, so the two leaflets face each other tails inward. On the right, a glycerophospholipid is drawn with a vertical glycerol backbone reading CH2, CH, CH2 from top to bottom. The topmost branch is printed in green and reads CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH2N(CH3)3+, tagged by a green arrow labeled "Ionic head". The two lower branches each run through O-C(=O) into a long tan ribbon of the same shade and waviness as the strands filling the slab, and a magenta label "Nonpolar tails" sends two arrows to their free ends. Matching the green and tan across the two halves lets the reader place each region of the drawn molecule at its position in the assembled sheet. The pairing accounts for how a long nonpolar tail bound to a polar ionic head drives aggregation into a bilayer that keeps hydrocarbon away from water.

elements: Left panel: rectangular lipid-bilayer slab drawn in perspective, long axis running screen-left to screen-right and receding to the upper right
Top leaflet: dense hexagonal-ish tiling of small green spheres covering the entire top face (polar head groups)
Bottom leaflet: identical tiling of green spheres covering the entire bottom face
Interior fill: pale tan wavy hydrocarbon strands hanging down from each top sphere and rising up from each bottom sphere
Midplane: tail tips of the two leaflets meeting tip-to-tip, leaving a faint horizontal seam through the slab center
Stepped cutaway notch at the near (front-left) corner of the slab: a rectangular block removed so the cross-section of heads / tails / midplane / tails / heads is exposed
Exposed cut faces showing head spheres in profile as a single row on each edge of the cut
Right panel: flat structural formula of a glycerophospholipid (phosphatidylcholine)
Vertical glycerol backbone labels, top to bottom: CH2, CH, CH2, connected by vertical black bonds
Top branch drawn in green: CH2—O—P with P=O double bond up-left, O− up-right, then —O—CH2CH2N(CH3)3 with + superscript on N
Green arrow and green label text 'Ionic head' pointing down-left to the phosphocholine group
Middle branch: CH—O—C with C=O double bond drawn upward, continuing into a long tan wavy ribbon (fatty-acyl chain) running to the right
Bottom branch: CH2—O—C with C=O double bond drawn upward, continuing into a second long tan wavy ribbon running to the right
Magenta label text 'Nonpolar tails' at right with two magenta arrows pointing to the free ends of the two tan ribbons
Highlight glow overlays (one per molecular region) usable on both panels

interactions.teaches: The membrane is a two-layer sheet with finite thickness: rotating shows heads paving both outer faces while the tails are hidden entirely inside.

interactions.label: Highlight region
interactions.teaches: Each named region of the single drawn molecule occupies one specific stratum of the assembled bilayer — head at the water-facing surfaces, glycerol at the head/tail boundary, tails in the core.

Clicking the phosphocholine group, the glycerol backbone, or a tan tail ribbon in the formula lights the corresponding layer of the slab (and vice versa), making the structure-to-assembly map explicit.

interactions.label: Cutaway depth
interactions.teaches: Slicing into the slab exposes, in order, the green head layer, the tan tail region, and the midplane where tail tips from the two leaflets touch — polar outside, nonpolar inside.

demo_steps.title: Intact membrane
demo_steps.narration: A slab of bilayer sits beside the glycerophospholipid that builds it. Only green head groups are visible from outside; the whole hydrocarbon interior is buried.

demo_steps.title: Ionic head at the surface
demo_steps.narration: Highlighting the phosphocholine group turns the green spheres on both faces of the slab: the charged head is what contacts water, on both sides of the membrane.

demo_steps.title: Cut into the core
demo_steps.narration: Opening the corner cutaway reveals the tan tails packed between the two head layers, and the seam at mid-thickness where tail tips from opposing leaflets meet.

demo_steps.title: Glycerol at the boundary
demo_steps.narration: The glycerol backbone and its two ester carbonyls sit exactly where green meets tan — the narrow interfacial band that joins the polar surface to the nonpolar interior.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Layout: two panels side by side, slab centered near x = -5.5, formula panel a flat billboard plane spanning x = +0.5 to +8.5, y = -3 to +3, facing the camera. SLAB: 7.0 (X, screen-right) x 2.2 (Y, thickness) x 4.5 (Z, receding) world units; long axis horizontal, receding edge toward upper right. Head spheres radius 0.13, center-to-center spacing 0.30, arranged on a 24 x 15 grid with slight row offset on both top face (y = +1.10) and bottom face (y = -1.10); sphere color green #4FBF8F with lighter highlight #8FD9B6, slightly translucent-glossy. Tails: for each head sphere, one wavy tan strand (tube radius 0.035, 3 gentle sinusoidal bends, amplitude ~0.08) running from the sphere toward the midplane y = 0, length 1.05 so opposing tips nearly touch at y = 0; tail color #D9A38E to #E5BCA9. Faint horizontal midplane seam line at y = 0 in #C98F7C. Cutaway: rectangular notch removed from the front-left corner, notch footprint grows with slider from 0 to 2.6 units in X and 1.8 units in Z, full height in Y; the cut walls show heads in profile and tails in cross-section. FORMULA (right panel, 2D, read top to bottom): backbone labels CH2 at y = +2.0, CH at y = 0.0, CH2 at y = -2.0, all at x = +1.2, black #1A1A1A text. Top branch runs horizontally right from CH2: 'CH2—O—P—O—CH2CH2N(CH3)3+' with P at x = +3.0; P=O double bond drawn up-left at ~120 deg, O- drawn up-right at ~60 deg; entire branch and the choline text in green #17A06A, the '+' as a superscript on N. Green arrow from label 'Ionic head' (text at x = +5.8, y = +3.3) descending left to the P—O—CH2 region. Middle branch from CH: '—O—C' with C at x = +3.4, C=O double bond drawn straight up (O at y = +0.9), then tan ribbon (width 0.13, 4 shallow waves) from x = +3.9 to x = +7.6 at y = -0.1. Bottom branch from lower CH2: same '—O—C' with C=O up, tan ribbon from x = +3.9 to x = +7.5 at y = -2.1. Magenta #E0218A label 'Nonpolar tails' at x = +8.6, y = -1.1 with two magenta arrows to the free right ends of both ribbons. Tan ribbon color must exactly match the slab tail color #D9A38E. Highlight glow: emissive boost + soft outline in the region's own hue (green #17A06A for head, amber #E8A33D for glycerol linker, magenta-tinted tan #E0218A outline on #D9A38E for tails), applied simultaneously to the formula region and the matching slab stratum (head = sphere layers, glycerol = thin band at |y| = 0.95-1.05, tails = all strands).
interactionPlan.notes: Render head spheres with a single InstancedMesh per leaflet (~360 instances each) using MeshPhysicalMesh/standard material with clearcoat for the glossy bead look; tails as InstancedMesh of a short CatmullRom TubeGeometry, or merged BufferGeometry, mirrored for the lower leaflet. Implement the cutaway with three THREE.Plane clipping planes (localClipping enabled) forming the notch corner rather than deleting instances, so the slider is continuous; add capped cut-face quads (or a stencil cap) tinted pale tan so the interior does not look hollow. Formula panel: draw once to a high-res CanvasTexture (subscripts/superscripts, arrows, wavy tan ribbons via quadratic curves) on a camera-facing plane, with separate transparent overlay canvases per highlight region toggled by opacity; hit-test clicks by unprojecting to the panel plane and comparing against stored region rectangles. Keep formula plane unlit (MeshBasicMaterial) on a white background so it reads as flat line art beside the shaded 3D slab; exclude it from orbit rotation by re-billboarding each frame. Soft directional key light from upper left plus hemisphere fill; no hard shadows.

- Click ionic head, glycerol linker, or nonpolar tails: the selected part highlights in the molecule and in the bilayer slab, mapping amphiphilic structure to membrane organization.

authoredContext:
Phospholipids are found widely in both plant and animal tissues and make up approximately 50% to 60% of cell membranes. Because they are like soaps in having a long, nonpolar hydrocarbon tail bound to a polar ionic head, phospholipids in the cell membrane organize into a lipid bilayer about 5.0 nm (50 Å) thick. As shown in the figure, the nonpolar tails aggregate in the center of the bilayer in much the same way that soap tails aggregate in the center of a micelle. This bilayer serves as an effective barrier to the passage of water, ions, and other components into and out of cells.

Aggregation of glycerophospholipids into the lipid bilayer that composes cell membranes.

Glycerophospholipids combine with the lipid bilayer comprising a cell membrane. An arrow points to the ionic head and two nonpolar tails of the lipid bilayer.

discrepancies: The formula panel overlaps the bilayer slab: the 'CH2' of the glycerol backbone and the leading 'O' sit on top of the slab's right edge, whereas in the source the two halves are cleanly separated side by side.

The bilayer slab's proportions differ — the source shows a long, thin, wide slab with a pronounced stepped cutaway at the front-left corner and visible tail strands in the exposed cross-section; the generated slab is more block-like and its cut face reads as a flat tan panel rather than showing tail cross-sections.

Head-group beads in the source are bright light-green spheres with strong specular highlights arranged in an obvious hexagonal/ordered carpet; the generated beads are darker, more muted teal-green and less distinctly bead-like at default zoom.
Source fatty-acyl tails are smooth, gently undulating thick ribbons with tapered ends; the generated ribbons are high-frequency sine wiggles that read more like springs than lipid chains.

The 'Nonpolar tails' magenta label in the source is large and placed to the right with two clearly divergent arrows; in the generated version the arrows are short and the label is smaller relative to the chemical formula text.

The 'Ionic head' green arrow in the source points down-left to the choline group from above; the generated arrow is present but very short and the callout sits close to the formula, reducing the source's clear annotation separation.
evaluation.notes: A well-constructed, genuinely 3D bilayer slab paired with a faithful phosphatidylcholine line formula and strong region-highlight/cutaway/guided-tour interactions; main weaknesses are the slab overlapping the formula's leftmost atoms, a blockier slab proportion with a flat cut face, and slightly off head-group color/tail waviness versus the source.
action_items: Shift the formula group further to the right (or shrink/reposition the slab) so no chemical symbols overlap the bilayer slab.
Make the slab wider and thinner with a clearer stepped corner cutaway, and render tail cross-sections on the exposed cut face instead of a flat tan panel.
Brighten the head-group spheres toward the source's light spring-green with stronger specular highlights, and lower the ribbon wave frequency so tails read as smooth undulating chains.
Enlarge the 'Ionic head' and 'Nonpolar tails' callouts relative to the atom labels and lengthen their arrows to match the source's annotation hierarchy.

discrepancies: In the source the cut faces of the slab clearly show hundreds of individual tan hydrocarbon tail strands packed between the two bead layers; in the render the interior reads as an almost featureless solid tan box, so the defining 'tails fill the core' visual is largely lost.
The stepped corner cutaway in the source is a pronounced L-shaped notch removing a big bite of the slab; the default 0.35 cut produces only a shallow step that is hard to read as a cutaway.

Slab proportions differ: the source slab is thicker and larger relative to the formula (roughly 1/3 of the figure width and visually dominant), while the rendered slab is small and thin compared with the oversized chemical formula panel.

The head-group beads in the source are large, glossy, closely packed spheres forming a visibly bumpy paved surface on both faces; here they are tiny dots, and the bottom leaflet is barely perceptible.
Tan acyl ribbons in the formula are drawn as a regular sine wave of uniform amplitude, whereas the source shows an irregular, organically kinked chain with varying thickness.
evaluation.notes: The chemical structure panel is a close, well-labelled reproduction and the interaction set (region highlighting, animated cutaway slider, 4-step guided tour, clickable regions) is rich and pedagogically apt; the main weakness is the 3D slab, which is too small and whose interior reads as a plain tan box rather than the densely packed tail strands visible on the source's cut faces.
action_items: Enlarge the slab (and/or shrink the formula panel) so the two halves are balanced as in the source, and increase slab thickness so the two leaflets read clearly.

Inset the pale core box further (or remove it on the cut walls) so individual tail tubes are visible on the exposed faces, and increase tail radius/contrast so the hydrocarbon interior looks fibrous like the source.

Increase the default cutaway depth (≈0.6) so the stepped L-notch is immediately recognizable at first load, and enlarge the head beads so both the top and bottom leaflets read as a bumpy sphere pavement.
Add irregularity to the formula tail ribbons (varying kink positions/amplitude) to match the hand-drawn chain look of the source.

feedback.rationale: The conceptual decomposition and interaction structure are sound; the issues are concrete rendering fixes—slab scale/thickness, visible tail tubes on cut faces, larger beads, deeper default cutaway, and formula ribbon styling.
